chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Sama'ah, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'When the people are numerous at Jam' and there is narrowness upon them, what should they be doing?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'They should be arising to go to the two narrow points (Ma'azim).'

key_terms.الْمَأْزَمَيْنِ: The two narrow points or constricted areas, referring to specific locations or directions to move towards to relieve crowding
key_terms.جَمْعٍ: Jam', the station where pilgrims gather before proceeding to Mina
key_terms.ضَاقَتْ: Narrowness or congestion, referring to the density of the crowd

ai.seo_question: What should pilgrims do when the crowd at Jam' becomes too dense and narrow?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* outlines the practical protocol for managing crowd density at the station of Jam' during Hajj, directing pilgrims to ascend to 'al-Ma'azim' (the two narrow points or elevated areas) to ease congestion. Scholarly commentary often interprets 'al-Ma'azim' as specific high-ground locations near the Jam' stones, emphasizing the Imam's guidance on maintaining order and facilitating the ritual of Rami al-Jamarat through spatial adjustment rather than force. This ruling highlights the flexibility within Shia jurisprudence to adapt ritual performance to physical circumstances while preserving the sanctity of the rites.
